verses.text: Moses’ father in law was named Jethro. Jethro was a priest of Midian. Moses took care of Jethro’s sheep. Moses led the sheep to the backside of the desert. He went to a mountain called Horeb, the mountain of God.
On that mountain, Moses saw the angel of the Lord in a burning bush. Moses saw that the bush was on fire, but it was not being destroyed.
Moses said to himself: I will go closer to the bush and see why the bush could continue burning without being burned up.
When the Lord saw Moses coming to look, God called to Moses from inside the bush and said: Moses, Moses. Moses said: Here I am.
The Lord said to Moses: Do not come closer. Take off your shoes because the place that you are standing on is holy ground.
I am the God of your fathers, the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob. Moses covered his face because Moses was afraid to look at God.
Then the Lord said to Moses: I have surely seen the troubles my people have suffered in Egypt. I have heard their cry because of their slave drivers, and I know their suffering.

I have come down to rescue my people from the Egyptians, and to bring them up out of that land into a good and spacious land, a land flowing with milk and honey — the home of the Canaanites, the Hittites, the Amorites, the Perizzites, the Hivites, and the Jebusites.
The cry of the Israelites has reached me, and I have seen how harshly the Egyptians treat them.
So now, go. I am sending you to Pharaoh, to bring my people, the Israelites, out of Egypt.
Moses said to God: I am not an important man. I can not go to Pharaoh and bring the children of Israel out of Egypt.
God answered Moses: I will be with you. And this will be the sign that I have sent you: when you have brought the people out of Egypt, you will worship God on this mountain.
Then Moses said to God: When I go to the Israelites and tell them, The God of your ancestors has sent me to you, they will ask, What is his name? What should I tell them?
Then God said to Moses: My name is I Am Who I Am. You must tell the Israelites: I Am has sent me to you.

God also said to Moses: You must tell the Israelites: The Lord, the God of your ancestors — the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob — has sent me to you. This will always be my name. It is how I want the Israelites to remember me from now on.

Go and gather the elders of Israel together and tell them: The Lord, the God of your ancestors — the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob — has appeared to me and said: I have surely visited you and have seen what has been done to you in Egypt.

God said: I have decided to bring you up out of the troubles you are suffering in Egypt, into the land of the Canaanites, the Hittites, the Amorites, the Perizzites, the Hivites, and the Jebusites — a land flowing with milk and honey.

The leaders of Israel will listen to you, Moses. Then you, Moses and the leaders must go to the king of Egypt and tell him: The Lord, the God of the Hebrews, has talked to us. We beg you, King, let us go into the desert 3 days journey. We want to sacrifice offerings to the Lord our God.
I know that the king of Egypt will not let you go unless a mighty hand forces him.
So I will stretch out my hand and strike Egypt with all the wonders I will do there. After that, the king will let you go.
I will make the people of Egypt friendly towards children of Israel, and the people of Egypt will give the children of Israel many gifts when you go.

Every woman of Israel will ask her Egyptian neighbor, and any woman living in her house, for silver jewelry, gold jewelry, and fine clothing. Then you will put these things on your sons and daughters. In this way you will plunder the Egyptians.

verses.text: Then the Lord said to Moses:
Tell the Israelites to go back to the town of Pi-Hahiroth and put up their tents there, between Migdol and the sea. They must camp near the sea and near Baal-Zephon.
Then Pharaoh will think that the Israelites do not know where to go. Pharaoh will say they are lost in the desert.

Pharaoh is stubborn, and Pharaoh will go after the Israelites and chase them. But I will defeat Pharaoh and his army. This will bring honor to me. Then the Egyptians will know that I am the Lord. The Israelites did what Moses told them.

When they told Pharaoh, the king of Egypt, that the Israelites had fled, Pharaoh and Pharaoh's officials said: We have made a mistake. We let the Israelites go and now they are not our slaves anymore.
So Pharaoh prepared his chariot and took his men with him.
Pharaoh took six hundred of his best men and all of his chariots. There was an officer in each chariot.
The Lord made Pharaoh, king of Egypt, stubborn. Pharaoh followed and chased the Israelites, but the Israelites were leaving with boldness.
The Egyptians with their war-chariots and the soldiers came near the Israelites, who were camping at the sea at PiHahiroth near BaalZephon.
When the Israelites saw Pharaoh and his army coming toward them, they were very afraid and cried to the Lord for help.
They said to Moses, Was it because there were no graves in Egypt that you brought us to the desert to die? What have you done to us by bringing us out of Egypt?

We told you this would happen! In Egypt we said, Please don't bother us. Let us stay and serve the Egyptians. It would have been better for us to stay and be slaves than to come out here and die in the desert.
But Moses answered the children of Israel, Don't be afraid! Don't run away! Stand where you are and watch the Lord save you today. You will never see these Egyptians again.
You will not have to do anything but stay calm. The Lord will do the fighting for you.”
Then the Lord said to Moses, Why are you still crying to me? Tell the Israelites to start moving.
You must lift up your staff and hold it out over the sea. The water will separate and there will be dry ground for the Israelites to walk on.
I will make the Egyptians stubborn and they will go after you. I will show that I am God who can do what I want to do with Pharaoh and his army and his war-chariots and all his men.
Then Egypt will know that I am the Lord. They will honor me when I defeat Pharaoh and his horse soldiers and chariots.

Then the angel of God moved to the back of the people. (The angel was usually in front of the people, leading them.) So the tall cloud moved from in front of the people and went to the back of the people.

In this way the cloud stood between the Egyptians and the Israelites. There was light for the Israelites. But there was darkness for the Egyptians. So the Egyptians did not come any closer to the Israelites that night.
Moses raised his hand over the Red Sea, and the Lord caused a strong wind to blow from the east. The wind blew all night long. The sea split, and the wind made the ground dry.
The Israelites went through the sea on dry land. The water was like a wall on their right and on their left.
Then all of Pharaoh's chariots and horse soldiers followed them into the sea.
Early that morning the Lord looked down from the tall cloud and column of fire at the Egyptian army. Then the Lord threw the Egyptian army into a panic.
The wheels of the chariots became stuck. It was very hard to control the chariots. The Egyptians shouted, Let's get out of here! The Lord is fighting against us. He is fighting for the Israelites.
Then the Lord told Moses, Raise your hand over the sea to make the water fall and cover the Egyptian chariots and horse soldiers.

Then Moses put up his hand over the sea and the water of the sea flowed back to where it had been before. The Egyptians wanted to run away but the flood of water went over the Egyptians, and that is how God drowned the Egyptians in the sea.
The water returned to its normal level and covered the chariots and horse soldiers. Pharaoh's army had been chasing the Israelites, but that army was destroyed. None of them survived!
But the Israelites crossed the sea on dry land. The water was like a wall on their right and on their left.
So that day the Lord saved the Israelites from the Egyptians. Later, the Israelites saw the dead bodies of the Egyptians on the shore of the Red Sea.
The Israelites saw the great power of the Lord when he defeated the Egyptians. So, the people feared and respected the Lord, and they began to trust the Lord and his servant Moses.

verses.text: The LORD said to Moses: Go to Pharaoh and say: The LORD says, Let my people go, so they can worship me.
If you refuse to let them go, I will punish your whole country with frogs.

The Nile River will fill with frogs. They will come up into your palace, into your bedroom, and onto your bed. They will come into the houses of your officials and your people. They will jump into your ovens and into your bread pans.
The frogs will jump on you, on your people, and on all your officials.
The LORD said to Moses: Tell Aaron to stretch out his hand with his walking stick over the rivers, the streams, and the ponds. Command the frogs to come up onto the land of Egypt.
Aaron stretched out his hand over the waters of Egypt, and the frogs came up and covered the whole land.
But the magicians used their occult magic tricks and did the same thing. They also made frogs come up onto the land of Egypt.
Then Pharaoh called for Moses and Aaron. He said: Beg the LORD to take the frogs away from me and my people. Then I will let your people go to offer sacrifices to the LORD.
Moses said to Pharaoh: You may set the time. Tell me when you want me to pray for you, your officials, and your people, so that the frogs will leave you and your houses, and stay only in the river.
Pharaoh said: Tomorrow. Moses said: It will happen just as you say. Then you will know that there is no one like the LORD our God.
The frogs will leave you, your houses, your officials, and your people. They will stay only in the river.
Moses and Aaron left Pharaoh, and Moses cried out to the LORD about the frogs He had brought against Pharaoh.
The LORD did what Moses asked. The frogs in the houses, the yards, and the fields all died.
The people piled the dead frogs into large heaps, and the whole land smelled terrible.
But when Pharaoh saw that the trouble was over, he made his own heart stubborn again. He would not listen to Moses and Aaron, just as the LORD had said.
Then the LORD said to Moses: Tell Aaron to stretch out his walking stick and strike the dust on the ground. The dust will turn into gnats through the whole land of Egypt.

Aaron and Moses did this. Aaron stretched out his hand with his walking stick and struck the dust of the earth. The dust became gnats on people and on animals. All the dust in Egypt turned into gnats.
The magicians tried to do the same thing with their secret tricks, but they could not make gnats. There were gnats on people and on animals everywhere.
The magicians said to Pharaoh: This is the finger of God! But Pharaoh's heart stayed stubborn. He would not listen to Moses and Aaron, just as the LORD had said.
The LORD said to Moses: Get up early in the morning and stand in front of Pharaoh when he goes out to the water. Say to him: The LORD says, Let my people go, so they can worship me.

If you will not let my people go, I will send large swarms of flies on you, your officials, your people, and your houses. The houses of the Egyptians will be full of flies, and even the ground will be covered with them.
But that day I will treat the land of Goshen differently. My people live there, and no flies will be found in that land. Then you will know that I, the LORD, am here in the middle of the land.
I will make a clear difference between my people and your people. This sign will happen tomorrow.
The LORD did this. Thick swarms of flies poured into Pharaoh's palace, into the houses of his officials, and into all the land of Egypt. The whole land was ruined because of the flies.
Pharaoh called for Moses and Aaron. He said: Go and offer sacrifices to your God here in this land.

Moses said: That would not be right. The Egyptian people worship cattle as sacred gods. If we sacrifice bulls in front of their eyes, the Egyptians will become furious and throw heavy stones to kill us!
We must travel three days into the desert and offer sacrifices to the LORD our God, just as He commands us.
Pharaoh said: I will let you go and offer sacrifices to the LORD your God in the desert. But do not go too far away. Now pray for me.

Moses said: As soon as I leave you, I will pray to the LORD. Tomorrow the flies will leave Pharaoh, his officials, and his people. But Pharaoh must not trick us again by refusing to let the people go and offer sacrifices to the LORD.
Moses left Pharaoh and prayed to the LORD.
The LORD did what Moses asked. He took away the swarms of flies from Pharaoh, his officials, and his people. Not one fly was left.
But Pharaoh made his heart stubborn again this time too, and he would not let the people go.

8.source: Drafted from the public-domain King James Version, checked verse-by-verse against the Hebrew text (Strong's Concordance / Blue Letter Bible) for word accuracy, reviewed for English-ASL clarity. Covers the second, third, and fourth plagues on Egypt: frogs, gnats, and flies, and Pharaoh's repeated pattern of hardening his own heart after each relief. Written with explicit nouns opening every verse, active voice, short sentences, no contractions, and plain vocabulary throughout (secret tricks for enchantments, walking stick for rod, stubborn for hardened heart). All pronouns referring to the LORD are capitalized per this site's standard.
